title: Саша переезжает к Максу и Косте  (Sasha Moves In with Max and Kostya)

segments.t: Feeling responsible for the flood, Max invites Sasha to move into his apartment with him and Kostya. Although Sasha first suspects he is only asking out of guilt, she happily accepts and starts kissing him right on the kitchen table as Kostya walks in.
Я сама разберусь со своими проблемами, правда.
Right, let's take their exchange slowly and unpack the Russian.
'Listen, I have been thinking.' Having been thinking is how Max lays out the situation for Kostya.
'Will you move in with me?' By asking whether Max moves in with him, Kostya presses Max for a straight answer.
'You just feel guilty.' Between the point and the truth, Max gives Kostya a quick, grounded response. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.
Я сама разберусь со своими проблемами, правда.
'I can handle my own problems myself, really.' Realizing that he can handle his own problems himself really changes how Kostya handles the situation.
'I am not asking because of that.' By being not asking, Max keeps his side of the story grounded.

'I have wanted to offer this to you for a long time.' Because he has wanted to offer this to Max for a long time, Kostya treats the matter as settled. Using the informal "you" shows how direct and unfiltered their kitchen relationship is.

'Well, are you sure about it yourself?' Asking whether Kostya sure about it themselves cuts straight through the tension between Max and Kostya. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.
'Why would I not be?' Wondering why he not be would is how Kostya puts Max on the spot.

'Why am I wasting time for nothing?' Turning from the apartment to the plan, Max asks Kostya directly. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.

'Maybe right here?' Around the kitchen and table, Kostya wants to know where Max really stands. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
'Do not mind me.' Max tells Kostya that do not mind him without dressing it up.
'I did not see you two.' Since he did not see Max two, Kostya does not waste words on excuses. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
'Kostik, close your eyes.' Between the plan and the shift, Max gives Kostya a quick, grounded response. Now let's listen to the entire scene again without interruption.
Я сама разберусь со своими проблемами, правда.
That wraps up this scene as max invites Sasha to move into his and Kostya's apartment, and she immediately makes herself at home while Kostya awkwardly walks in on them. Until next time!
